title: US BIS Reviews Chinese AI Firms' Offshore Access to Nvidia Chips via Overseas Cloud Rentals
detail: The Bureau of Industry and Security's enforcement arm is reviewing how Chinese AI firms — including Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, and Moonshot AI — access Nvidia hardware overseas by renting compute in third countries, Bloomberg and TheNextWeb reported August 7. BIS is compiling two lists: one tracking smuggling routes for restricted chips moving physically into China, and a second identifying countries where Chinese firms access Nvidia chips remotely via cloud rental — a arrangement that is not currently illegal under existing Export Administration Regulations, since BIS's authority centers on the physical movement of goods rather than cloud-computing access. The review follows a Bloomberg investigation (July 31) confirming Moonshot AI has a compute agreement with investor Alibaba for roughly 20,000 Hopper-generation Nvidia chips accessed via Malaysia-based intermediaries, and was triggered by Moonshot's Kimi K3 model posting benchmark scores close to the latest Anthropic and OpenAI systems despite official export restrictions. The House has passed bipartisan legislation to extend BIS authority to cloud-compute arrangements, but Senate passage remains uncertain. Nvidia said in response that export controls have caused it to 'forfeit the world's second-largest commercial market to foreign competitors,' warning 'America cannot afford to lose all of Asia next.'

media.caption: BIS is mapping how Chinese AI firms like Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and Moonshot access Nvidia chips overseas through offshore cloud rentals, a regulatory gray zone
